thesis: The Assurance Score rolls the repository's pre-deployment evidence into one reproducible number — static verification, exploit-replay resistance, and the traceability of every security-review finding to a re-runnable check. It is a worked demonstration of one design response — recomputing assurance on every commit — to the open empirical question both cited papers raise about audit effectiveness. The "continuous, multi-layered" framing is this project's, not a claim of either paper.

research.citation: Bourveau, Brendel & Schoenfeld (2024), Decentralized Finance (DeFi) assurance: early evidence (Review of Accounting Studies 29(3))
research.claim: Hand-codes ~8,500 DeFi audit reports; documents the market as pervasive, value-relevant, and substantively different from conventional financial audits.

research.citation: Landsman, Lyandres, Maydew, Rabetti & Zhang (2025), Auditing Smart Contracts (SSRN)
research.claim: Across ~8,195 reports and 1,575 protocols, finds post-deployment outcomes depend on auditor characteristics (market share, launch rate, hack rate) rather than on the mere presence of an audit.

components.label: Exploit Resistance
components.detail: 7/7 exploit classes resisted (6 prevented, 1 detected, 0 missed)

findings.title: Demo insolvency backdoor isolated to a separate contract
Full-close repayment could erode the solvency margin by one wei
Liquidation seizing all collateral must clear the full debt
Sustained interest can make a lender redemption exceed idle cash
Deeply under-water positions can leave residual bad debt
Share price is immune to direct token donations
A full-close repayment may charge up to one wei above userDebt()

scenarios.name: Privileged solvency break
scenarios.reference: Admin-key class: a privileged role mutates protocol accounting directly, as in forced-mint and forced-debt incidents.
scenarios.description: The attacker calls the demo-only attack() entrypoint on AttackableVault, inflating totalSupplyAssets so lender claims exceed the assets backing them. The production Vault has no such function; this scenario exists to prove INV-01 catches the resulting insolvency.

scenarios.name: ERC-4626 first-depositor inflation
scenarios.reference: ERC-4626 inflation attack class: an attacker donates assets to skew the shares-to-assets ratio so a later depositor is diluted to zero shares.
scenarios.description: The attacker seeds the vault with 1 wei, donates 9,000 tokens directly, then a victim deposits and redeems. The vault prices shares off stored totalSupplyAssets, not the token balance, so a direct donation cannot move the ratio and the victim redeems in full.

scenarios.name: Bad-debt collateral strip
scenarios.reference: Bad-debt class: a borrower removes collateral while keeping debt open, leaving the protocol with unbacked liabilities.
scenarios.description: A borrower deposits 10,000, borrows the full 8,000 cap, then attempts to withdraw all shares. Vault.withdraw re-checks the collateral cap on the post-withdrawal balance and reverts with CollateralCapExceeded.

scenarios.name: Reserve liquidity drain
scenarios.reference: Reserve-mismatch class: outstanding borrows exceed idle reserves and an LP redemption cannot be honoured.
scenarios.description: Three LPs deposit 150,000, a borrower drains the maximum 40,000, then an LP withdraws their full 50,000. Free liquidity (110,000) provably stays above any single LP balance, so the withdrawal succeeds; were it not, withdraw reverts with InsufficientLiquidity rather than corrupting state.

scenarios.name: Over-borrow beyond collateral cap
scenarios.reference: Undercollateralised-loan class: a borrower draws more debt than their collateral backs.
scenarios.description: A borrower with 10,000 collateral requests 8,000 + 1 wei, exceeding the 80% cap. Vault.borrow reverts with CollateralCapExceeded before any state changes.

scenarios.name: Interest-driven liquidation
scenarios.reference: Liquidation-cascade class: borrower interest outruns collateral value until the position is insolvent and must be cleared.
scenarios.description: A borrower draws the full 8,000 cap; two years of accrued interest pushes the debt past the collateral cap. A third-party liquidator repays the debt and seizes collateral plus the 5% bonus. All six invariants hold throughout; liquidation is the designed, solvency-preserving response.

scenarios.name: Rounding-dust extraction
scenarios.reference: Dust-drain class: an attacker loops tiny deposits/withdrawals to harvest favourable rounding.
scenarios.description: The attacker runs 50 single-wei deposit/withdraw cycles. Mint and redeem both floor-divide toward the protocol, so no value is extracted across any number of loops.
